items.prompt: A support assistant uses stable safety instructions, a tenant policy that becomes effective immediately when published, and a different customer question on every request. How should the application arrange the cached prefix?
constraints: Every answer must use the currently effective policy.
The common instructions are unchanged across these requests.

options.text: Cache safety instructions and the policy at a breakpoint; rebuild that prefix from current policy content and place each question after it.
Cache safety instructions and the first policy version for the session; apply policy updates when the session next starts.
Place each customer question before the policy breakpoint so the entire answered request becomes the reusable prefix.
Cache the policy separately from the prompt and use its cache-hit status to determine which policy version is effective.

feedback.Reason: A reusable prefix must contain the actual current policy bytes, while the changing question should not invalidate the common prefix.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Prompt caching matches the cumulative prefix at a breakpoint; changed content before that breakpoint produces a different prefix.
Details.scenarioApplication: Assemble stable safety content, then the current versioned policy, then the breakpoint and changing question. A policy change creates a different cumulative prefix.
Details.errorCorrection: Session pinning violates immediate effectiveness; changing questions before the breakpoint reduce reuse; cache status does not establish policy authority.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A policy update may incur a cold prefix before subsequent matching requests reuse it.
Details.transfer: Derive prompt content from current authoritative state and use caching to optimize repeated bytes.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: A session can continue under superseded policy after publication, violating the stated effectiveness rule.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Different questions change the cumulative prefix before the breakpoint and prevent reuse of the intended common content.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Cache availability cannot determine the authoritative policy version; the application must select current policy content first.

items.prompt: An application caches role instructions and tool schemas. A release adds a required tool parameter, after which the first request misses the cache and subsequent identical-prefix requests hit. What response fits this evidence?
constraints: The executor already enforces the new schema.
Live user queries follow the cached prefix.

options.text: Restore the old model-facing tool schema and translate omitted parameters in the executor to preserve the previous prefix.
Move the tool definitions behind each user query and investigate whether shorter role instructions restore the former hit rate.
Keep the updated model and executor schemas aligned, accept the changed prefix’s initial miss, and observe reuse on matching requests.
Roll back the schema release until the former cached prefix expires, then retry deployment with the same parameter requirement.

feedback.Reason: The schema change changes prefix content. An initial miss followed by matching-prefix hits is consistent with normal cache behavior, while model and executor contracts must remain aligned.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Prompt caching reuses matching prefix content; a changed tool or prompt block before the breakpoint creates a distinct prefix.
Details.scenarioApplication: Send the new tool schema with the stable instructions, retain the query after the breakpoint, and compare cache behavior for requests with the same new prefix.
Details.errorCorrection: Restoring an obsolete schema or delaying a valid release treats cache reuse as more authoritative than the tool contract.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Frequently changing schemas reduce reuse; stabilize genuine interface contracts without concealing required changes.
Details.transfer: Distinguish expected cache invalidation from a tool-contract defect.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The model would still see an obsolete interface and could omit a parameter the executor requires; preserving prefix bytes does not repair that mismatch.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: The changing query would become part of the preceding content and reduce reuse rather than explaining the observed successful warm requests.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: The new schema necessarily creates different prefix content regardless of when the former cache entry expires.

items.prompt: Several teams need a reusable procedure with instructions, reference files, and validation scripts. Startup should expose only a short description; detailed instructions and resources should load when relevant. Which packaging best matches that requirement?
constraints: Most requests do not need this procedure.
The procedure includes both guidance and executable resources.

options.text: Embed the complete procedure and reference text in the shared system prompt, and expose validation through a separate tool.
Package an Agent Skill with discoverable metadata, SKILL.md instructions, and supporting resources loaded as needed.
Store every procedure in a retrieval index and make semantic search the required first step of each conversation.
Provide a tool whose description contains all procedure instructions, with the reference files included in every tool result.

feedback.Reason: Skills support progressive disclosure of metadata, instructions, and resources, matching the requested reusable package and context-loading behavior.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Skills expose metadata first, load instructions when triggered, and load resources as needed.
Details.scenarioApplication: Describe when the Skill applies in metadata, put the workflow in SKILL.md, and include the relevant scripts and reference files for access when needed.
Details.errorCorrection: Always-loaded prompts and full tool descriptions impose unnecessary context costs; universal retrieval does not directly provide the requested packaged workflow.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If only a remote action interface were needed, a tool could be sufficient; this case requires reusable procedural instructions and resources.
Details.transfer: Choose a reusable unit whose loading behavior fits when its instructions and resources are needed.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The complete procedure loads even on unrelated requests, violating the small startup footprint.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Mandatory search on every conversation adds an unnecessary step and does not itself define the requested instruction-and-script package.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: The complete description and repeated references defeat the requirement to load detailed material only when relevant.

items.prompt: A platform serves several teams with the same role and output contract. Each team also has a specialized procedure with instructions and scripts, needed only for routed tasks. Which choices preserve reuse while limiting unnecessary context? Select TWO.
constraints: Common instructions are identical across teams.
Specialized procedures are selected only when relevant.

options.text: Keep the common role and output contract in a reusable prompt module before changing task content.
Append every team’s full procedure to the common prefix so any later task can use it without loading another file.
Copy the common role and output contract into each procedure and let each team revise its copy independently.
Expose specialized procedures as discoverable Skills and load their instructions and resources when selected.
Replace specialized procedure instructions with script names and rely on the model to infer each team’s workflow.

feedback.Reason: The shared contract benefits from a common module, while specialized procedures benefit from progressive disclosure rather than universal inclusion.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Skills load needed files and bundle instructions, resources, and scripts without imposing their context cost before access.
Details.scenarioApplication: Assemble the common role and output instructions consistently, then route relevant tasks to Skills that provide the specific workflow and resources.
Details.errorCorrection: Universal inclusion wastes context, independent copies drift, and script names do not replace required procedural guidance.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A procedure used on virtually every request might justify more upfront context; the stated procedures are selectively needed.
Details.transfer: Separate genuinely shared instructions from task-specific procedures according to their reuse and loading needs.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Unrelated team procedures consume context on every request, contrary to selective loading.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Independent copies weaken the single shared contract and make consistency harder to maintain.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.e: Names alone omit the workflow decisions and constraints supplied by the specialized instructions.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.a: The identical role and output contract should remain a shared reusable module.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.d: Skills provide the on-demand instructions and resources required for specialized procedures.

items.prompt: A service shares identical safety instructions across tenants, but each tenant has private, independently versioned entitlement rules. The application has validated the tenant identity before assembling the prompt. How should it combine correct policy selection with prefix reuse?
constraints: Answers must use the requesting tenant’s current entitlement policy.
A customer question changes on every request.

options.text: Select a recently cached entitlement policy with the same product tier, then append the validated tenant identity as a correction.
Use one shared entitlement summary for the cacheable portion and let the model resolve tenant-specific exceptions from the question.
Pin each tenant to its first policy prefix for the session and refresh only after the user explicitly asks about a policy change.
Assemble the current policy for the validated tenant after the common safety content, with the changing question after the cache breakpoint.

feedback.Reason: The application must select the correct tenant and policy version before caching can optimize matching prefix content. Reuse does not establish authorization or policy freshness.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Prompt caching reuses matching cumulative prefixes; placing tenant policy before the breakpoint makes version changes visible, while tenant scoping and privacy are requirements supplied by this scenario.
Details.scenarioApplication: Resolve the policy using validated tenant identity and current version, assemble its actual content with the common instructions, and put the question after the breakpoint.
Details.errorCorrection: Product-tier similarity, model inference, and session pinning do not satisfy the requirement for current tenant-specific entitlement rules.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Different tenant policy content may reduce shared-prefix reuse; preserve policy correctness rather than substituting another tenant’s content.
Details.transfer: Treat tenant scoping and freshness as application responsibilities, and cache only the correctly assembled request content.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A policy for the same product tier may have different private entitlements; an appended identity does not correct the selected policy.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: A common summary can omit tenant-specific rules, and the customer question is not an authoritative source of those rules.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Session pinning can retain a superseded entitlement policy even after the tenant’s current version changes.

items.prompt: A shopping assistant uses stable role instructions and an output schema, weekly examples, an hourly catalog, and a different question each time. Each layer receives enough repeated requests to benefit from reuse. What arrangement best preserves useful prefixes as content changes?
constraints: The current catalog must be used immediately after publication.
The request supports cache breakpoints at appropriate content boundaries.

options.text: Place the latest question first, followed by the catalog, examples, and role contract, with a breakpoint after the entire request.
Order content from stable contract through examples to current catalog, set breakpoints for reusable prefixes, and put the question last.
Cache the contract, examples, and catalog as a single session-pinned prefix and apply all updates together at the weekly boundary.
Put the hourly catalog before the stable instructions and cache only the complete prefix so every content layer has one refresh policy.

feedback.Reason: Ordering stable content before more volatile content preserves reusable earlier prefixes while current catalog bytes and the final question change independently.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends placing static tools, system instructions, context, and examples before dynamic content and adding a breakpoint after the stable prefix.
Details.scenarioApplication: Place the stable role and schema first, then weekly examples, then the current catalog with suitable breakpoints, and append the changing question after those reusable portions.
Details.errorCorrection: A changing question or catalog before stable material changes the cumulative prefix; session pinning also violates catalog freshness.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Breakpoints are useful only where matching prefixes recur; measure reuse rather than adding boundaries to content that rarely repeats.
Details.transfer: Arrange prompt content by stability while maintaining current authoritative data.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The changing question invalidates the cumulative prefix from its beginning, preventing reuse of the intended stable content.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Waiting for a weekly refresh serves an outdated hourly catalog and violates immediate publication requirements.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: An hourly catalog change before the stable instructions changes the cumulative prefix that includes those instructions.

items.prompt:
A customer-support prompt prepends a fresh customer transcript, cart, exchange rate, and request-specific entitlement on every turn. Only a 100-token safety header is stable, below the selected provider’s documented prompt-cache eligibility minimum, and padding it with repeated text would add cost without adding useful task content.

Which cache decision is correct for this prompt shape?
constraints: The transcript, cart, exchange rate, and entitlement change on every turn.
Only a 100-token safety header is stable, below the selected provider's documented eligibility minimum.
Padding would add tokens without useful content; current authorization state must remain explicit.

options.text: Repeat static phrases or place the volatile customer state before a breakpoint to reach the cache threshold and maximize prompt reuse.
Treat the stable header's occasional match as a cacheable contract and report prompt savings even when the request-specific prefix changes.
Drop the current entitlement and cart from the prompt so a generic support template can be cached for every customer.
Keep current state explicit, avoid padding, and accept no cache prefix until stable eligible content exists.

feedback.Reason: Prompt reuse depends on exact stable bytes and provider eligibility; forcing a cache breakpoint around volatile state creates misses and token cost rather than safe reuse.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Prompt caching matches the cumulative prefix at a breakpoint; changed content before that breakpoint produces a different prefix. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: There is no worthwhile eligible stable prefix to cache in this prompt shape, so the design must preserve current authorization state and avoid padding or moving volatile data into a purported cache prefix.
Details.scenarioApplication: Keep the safety header and current user state in their explicit roles, do not pad the prompt or claim cache reuse, and accept the absence of an eligible cache prefix until a genuinely stable contract or policy block exists.
Details.errorCorrection: Repeated padding does not make the changing transcript, cart, rate, or entitlement stable; exact-prefix comparison will miss and the extra tokens increase cost.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a versioned role and policy block became stable and long enough for provider eligibility, place that exact block before the breakpoint and keep per-request state after it.
Details.transfer: Use measured slice quality, service limits, and authority boundaries together; choose the least complex route that clears every stated floor and revisit it when the evidence changes.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Repeated padding does not make the changing state stable; exact-prefix comparison will miss and the extra tokens increase cost.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: The header is below the provider eligibility minimum, and a matching fragment does not establish an eligible reusable prefix for the complete request.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Removing request-specific authorization and state would make the prompt incomplete and unsafe; cache eligibility cannot justify deleting required inputs.

items.prompt:
A policy release changes the current support policy from P41 to P42. Cache-hit rate remains 92%, but 0.6% of responses cite P41 after rollout; a trace of the actually assembled request shows the application still fetched and placed P41 before the cache breakpoint.

Where should the team repair the stale-policy behavior?
constraints: The current policy is P42, but traces show the application assembled P41 before the cache breakpoint.
Provider caching compares exact prefix bytes; a request assembled with P42 would not match the old P41 prefix.
The application can trace fetched revision, assembled prefix revision, cache outcome, and response outcome and canary the fix.

options.text: Repair current-policy fetch and assembly, then canary actual policy revision and outcome while preserving provider cache behavior.
Invalidate the provider cache or blame prompt caching because the 92% hit rate suggests stale content was reused.
Keep P41 before the breakpoint until its cache entries expire, then annotate responses as P42 while the application migration completes.
Put P42 after the existing P41 breakpoint so the stable prefix continues to hit, and rely on the response text to reflect the new policy.

feedback.Reason: Exact-prefix semantics turn the observed P41 assembly into the decisive evidence: current P42 bytes would naturally miss the P41 prefix, so application freshness is the repair boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Prompt caching reuses matching prefix content; a changed tool or prompt block before the breakpoint creates a distinct prefix. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The stale response is an application policy-fetch/assembly defect; repair current-policy selection before the cache call and use version/outcome joins to prove the fix.
Details.scenarioApplication: Fix the policy fetch and assembly path to place current P42 bytes before the breakpoint, canary responses with the actual assembled revision and outcome, and retain provider cache behavior; do not claim the unchanged provider cache served changed bytes.
Details.errorCorrection: The provider compares exact prefix bytes; the trace already shows the application supplied P41, so provider invalidation would not repair the stale fetch path and would hide the root cause.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the assembled request showed P42 but responses still cited P41, inspect downstream retrieval or response attribution; if P42 bytes were never assembled, keep the repair at the application policy source.
Details.transfer: Use measured slice quality, service limits, and authority boundaries together; choose the least complex route that clears every stated floor and revisit it when the evidence changes.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: The trace already identifies P41 in the application request; provider invalidation would not repair the stale fetch path and would hide the root cause.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Annotating a response does not change the assembled policy bytes; serving P41 during the P42 release leaves the application defect in place.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Placing current policy after a stale prefix still sends P41 as governing context; preserving a hit cannot override exact-prefix freshness or policy authority.
